title: 26 CFR 1.170A-1 Charitable, etc., contributions and gifts; allowance of deduction
summary: Contribution is made when delivery is effected; mailed check that clears is made on mailing date; endorsed stock certificate on delivery/mailing; certificate delivered to donor's bank/broker/issuer for transfer is complete on the date transferred on the corporation's books.

title: Publication 526 (2025), Charitable Contributions
pinpoint: 'When To Deduct' (checks, text message, credit card, pay-by-phone, stock certificate, promissory note); 'Contributions to Donor-Advised Funds'; 'Contemporaneous written acknowledgment'
summary: Credit card gifts deductible in year charged; pay-by-phone gifts delivered when the financial institution pays; DAF gift requires CWA stating sponsor has exclusive legal control; CWA must be received by earlier of filing date or due date.

title: 26 U.S.C. §170(f)(8) and (f)(18)
summary: CWA required for gifts >= $250, must state cash amount and description (not value) of noncash property and goods/services; DAF gifts deductible only with CWA that sponsor has exclusive legal control over contributed assets.

title: Publication 561, Determining the Value of Donated Property (Rev. Dec 2025)
pinpoint: 'Stocks and Bonds' - selling prices on valuation date; no-sales weighted average rule
summary: For actively traded securities, donor's FMV is the mean of the high and low quoted selling prices on the valuation date; weighted-average rule when no sales on that date. This is a donor tax-valuation rule, distinct from GAAP fair value.

title: Differentiating Unauthorized Return Reasons (Nacha Operating Rules change)
summary: R11 (error in authorized consumer debit) has a 60-day return timeframe (previously 2-day); confirms extended consumer-debit return windows far exceed a 5-business-day window. R10 60-day window not stated on this page (known from rules, not verified here).

title: Charitable year-end tax deadlines
summary: Sponsor guideline: mailed checks need USPS postmark/receipt by Dec 31; EFT must be initiated by 11:59 pm ET Dec 31; wires and securities must be received by Dec 31. Labeled as guidelines, not tax advice.

title: Fidelity Charitable Program Guidelines (Terms and Conditions), CGF-PC-04/24
pinpoint: Contributions - General (p.[5]); Costs associated with contributions (p.[6]); Fees and Expenses (Minimums; General operating expenses)
summary: Contributions not accepted until Trustees deem so; declined property returned; accepted contributions irrevocable with exclusive legal control. Admin fee 0.60% of average assets or $100 minimum, charged daily to pools, shortfall to $100 assessed at fiscal year end; UBIT and other contribution costs may be allocated to the Giving Account.

title: Fidelity Investments Charitable Gift Fund Consolidated Financial Statements FY ended June 30, 2025 and 2024
pinpoint: Note 2: Basis of Accounting (available to be issued Oct 29, 2025); Net Assets Without/With Donor Restrictions; Donor Contributions; Receivable for Tier Price Credit; Liquidity; Income Taxes; Investments (independent pricing services approved by Trustees)
summary: Contributions recorded on date received and accepted; donors have no legal or beneficial interest in sub-accounts; NA without restrictions $85.8B, with restrictions $89M incl. accounts with donor-imposed limitations; fee charged on daily net asset basis; pays UBIT; subsequent events through available-to-be-issued date.

title: Vanguard Charitable Endowment Program Financial Statements FY ended June 30, 2025 and 2024
pinpoint: Note 2 Donor Contributions; Grants; Net Assets Without Donor Restrictions; Note 7 Net Assets Released for Administrative Fee; Note 8 Income Taxes
summary: Contribution revenue when an 'in good order' unconditional promise is accepted; grants expensed when authorized; DAFs are net assets without donor restrictions; 0.60% admin fee accrued daily, reduces pool NAV, presented as net assets released (not revenue); pays UBIT on certain illiquid contributions.

title: Colorado Gives Foundation Consolidated Financial Report December 31, 2025
pinpoint: Note 2: Agency Endowments and Designations; Grants; Income Taxes; Note 7
summary: Agency endowments/designations (nonprofit transfers naming itself beneficiary) are liabilities ($69.7M); unconditional grants expensed and payable when approved; conditional grants when conditions substantially met; UBIT estimated and recognized in the period the return is filed.

title: Boston Foundation, Inc. Consolidated Financial Statements June 30, 2025 and 2024
pinpoint: Note 1/2 net asset groups (variance power paragraph); (i) Grants Expense; (j) Contributions; (l) Administrative Fees
summary: Variance power causes all funds except perpetual endowments to be classified without donor restrictions; grants without substantive conditions accrued when approved by Board or committed to grantees; admin fees allocated to operating fund based on market value (internal).

title: Foundation for the Carolinas Consolidated Financial Statements December 31, 2025 and 2024
pinpoint: Statement of Activities; Note 2 Contributions, Administrative Fees Received, Income Taxes; Note 9 Grants payable
summary: Grants recorded when approved and all conditions met; admin fees assessed monthly on fair value, recognized in year they occur, $7.0M reported as revenue on $4.4B net assets (consistent with internal fees eliminated); agency gifts/grants netted out of revenue/expense.

title: ASU 2018-08 Not-for-Profit Entities (Topic 958): Clarifying the Scope and the Accounting Guidance for Contributions Received and Contributions Made
effective_date: resource providers (non-PBE): annual periods beginning after 2019-12-15
summary: Conditional contribution needs barrier plus right of return/release; ambiguous stipulations presumed conditional; applies to contributions made; 720-25-25-1: unconditional promises recognized as payables and expense in period made. Superseded 958-720-25-2 had said recognition generally occurs when donor approves a specific grant or recipient is notified.

title: FASB Statement No. 136, Transfers of Assets to a Not-for-Profit Organization or Charitable Trust That Raises or Holds Contributions for Others
source_type: accounting standard (pre-Codification; codified in ASC 958-605 and 958-20)
pinpoint: paras 11, 12 (variance power definition), 17(a)-(d), 18, 19; Appendix A Example paras 53-56
summary: Recipient is a donee if donor explicitly grants variance power (unilateral power to redirect, referenced in transfer instrument). Transfer is a liability of recipient if provider can redirect, transfer is revocable/repayable, provider controls recipient, or provider names itself/affiliate as beneficiary (para 17(d)) - Example: liability even though variance power granted.

title: ASU 2016-14 Not-for-Profit Entities (Topic 958): Presentation of Financial Statements of Not-for-Profit Entities
summary: All NFPs present expenses by nature and function in one place; disclose allocation methods among program and support functions, and income tax expense with nature of activities generating it; liquidity disclosures of financial assets available within one year, considering internal board limits.

title: Instructions for Schedule D (Form 990) (Rev. 12/2024, continuous use)
effective_date: tax year 2024 and later until superseded
pinpoint: Part I (DAF definition, Exceptions, lines 1-4); Part X line 2; Parts XI-XII
summary: Lines 2-4 report 'aggregate value' of contributions to, grants from, and year-end value of DAFs; line 3 includes grants outside and transfers within the organization; DAFs not limited to GAAP 'funds'; no measurement basis specified; Parts XI-XII reconcile to audited ASC 958 statements; Part X refers to ASC 740 footnote.

title: Instructions for Form 990 (2025)
pinpoint: General Instructions 'Accounting method'; Part IX Statement of Functional Expenses introduction
summary: Return should generally use the same accounting method used for books and records; Part IX uses the organization's normal accounting method; if the system doesn't allocate expenses, any reasonable allocation method may be used, reported accurately and documented in records.

title: Instructions for Form 990-T (2025)
pinpoint: Who Must File; When To File; estimated tax section
summary: File if gross UBI >= $1,000; due 15th day of 5th month after year end; installment payments of estimated tax required if estimated tax is expected to be $500 or more.

title: Journal of Accountancy, Dec 2009, on ASU 2009-06 (Income Taxes: implementation guidance on uncertainty)
summary: ASU 2009-06 clarified all entities are subject to Topic 740 even if the only tax position is status; tax-exempt NFPs must also evaluate positions such as recognition of unrelated business income. Secondary; Codification text not read.

title: FASB Statement No. 154, Accounting Changes and Error Corrections
summary: Error in prior-period statements discovered after issuance is reported as a prior-period adjustment by restating prior statements: cumulative effect to opening net assets of first period presented, period-specific effects corrected, with disclosure. Materiality governs applicability (no numeric threshold).

title: FASB Statement No. 165, Subsequent Events
source_type: accounting standard (pre-Codification; codified in ASC 855, later amended by ASU 2010-09)
summary: Statements are 'issued' when widely distributed and 'available to be issued' when complete and all approvals obtained; entities other than public entities (incl. conduit bond obligors) evaluate subsequent events through available-to-be-issued date; recognized subsequent events adjust statements.

title: SEC Staff Accounting Bulletin No. 99, Materiality
jurisdiction: US (SEC registrants; persuasive only for NFPs)
summary: Notes the 5% rule of thumb but states exclusive reliance on any percentage or numerical threshold has no basis in accounting literature or law; qualitative factors required.

title: ISA 320 Materiality in Planning and Performing an Audit, application material
issuer: IAASB (text hosted by Chartered Accountants Ireland)
source_type: auditing standard (international; AU-C 320 is the converged AICPA equivalent, not itself fetched)
summary: Auditor may consider 1% of total revenue or total expenses appropriate for a not-for-profit entity, while higher or lower percentages may be appropriate in the circumstances; percentages are judgment-based planning benchmarks, not thresholds for entity controls.

title: 15 U.S.C. §80a-3(c)(10) (Investment Company Act exclusion for charitable organizations and their pooled funds)
summary: Charitable organizations and pooled/collective funds they maintain exclusively for investment of charitable assets are excluded from the definition of investment company, so registered-fund NAV/valuation rules do not apply to DAF investment pools.

title: Good Faith Determinations of Fair Value (Rule 2a-5) final rule page
summary: For registered funds, board or valuation designee must assess valuation risk, select/apply/test methodologies and oversee pricing services. Not applicable to DAF sponsors; a design analog for delegated, exception-based valuation oversight.

title: Accounting for Agency Endowment Funds Held at Community Foundations; FAQ: Agency Endowment Funds
effective_date: last updated 2010; page notes outdated, updated 2025 with Baker Tilly
pinpoint: Accounting page (FAS 136 App A Ex. 9 para 56; para 19); FAQ page https://cof.org/content/faq-agency-endowment-funds
summary: Community foundation recognizes a liability and nonprofit an asset for agency endowments (reciprocal transfer); National Standards for U.S. Community Foundations require variance power in fund agreements; agency vs third-party gifts in hybrid funds may be accounted for differently.

title: KPMG Defining Issues Aug 2018: FASB adds Concepts Statement guidance on materiality
summary: Reports FASB amended Concepts Statement 8 Chapter 3 (Aug 2018) to restore the pre-existing materiality definition consistent with SEC/AICPA/courts; prior text said FASB cannot specify a uniform quantitative threshold. Not fetched; do not rely on exact wording.

title: How to Account for Verbal Promises to Give
summary: A promise is recognized when there is sufficient verifiable documentation that a promise was made and received; unconditional intention that is legally enforceable. Secondary support that a promise involves a recipient receiving it (communication).
